Plan step 1 measurements, 2026-10-31, on a copy of the live bindings.json (23.5 MB, 5,664 bindings), origin/main d74d53a5ffd, each run in its own process, tracemalloc peak:
- Top-level keys: bindings 22.16 MB serialized (94%), comment_ids 0.24 MB, reverse 0.20 MB (0.8%), version. Writer is binding_repository.py json.dump(indent=2, sort_keys=True) via mkstemp + os.replace.
- Current binding_jira_key_map: 67.1 MB peak, 0.11 s (2 runs). Reproduces the observation (66.4 MB on the 22.1 MB file).
- Prototype A, format-coupled seek (mmap, rfind the top-level indent-2 reverse key, raw_decode only that value): 1.3 MB peak, 0.017 s, identical map. Behaviour difference found: a file with a git conflict marker inserted inside the bindings section returns {} today and the full 5,664-entry map under A, so the documented corrupt-store -> {} contract does not hold.
- Prototype B, full validating parse with an object_pairs_hook that discards every non-leaf object: 47.0 MB peak, 0.11 s, identical map, corrupt-store contract kept.
- Option C, per-process cache keyed on (mtime_ns, size): first call per process is the current 67.1 MB; later calls in the same process skip the parse until the file changes. CLI searches are one call per process, so C changes nothing there; it helps the long-lived MCP server.
Per-call loads: search_state calls binding_jira_key_map once per search; resolve_ticket_id loads the file once per Jira-key-shaped id (_JIRA_KEY_RE), including search's parent_resolver when the parent filter is a Jira key.
The remedy choice is paused pending an operator decision: A trades the corrupt-store contract for the largest cut, B keeps the contract for a smaller cut, C keeps the contract and only removes repeat loads.

Plan-review advisories: (1) composer_edit._enforce_promote_only also calls binding_jira_key_map; it only tests membership in the fresh dict that function builds per call, so the cached reverse map is never exposed or mutated there, and freshness is the same stat-token check as every other caller. (2) Cache concurrency: a populate race in a threaded server is benign; both writers store an equal map for the same token and single dict assignment is atomic under the GIL, matching the _TOML_CACHE precedent. (3) The mechanism-delta ratchet exits 0 with no marker; a module-level cache dict is not one of its 7 censused kinds.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
`_load_binding_reverse` in `src/rebar/_ids.py` `json.load`s the whole `.tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/bindings.json` only to read its top-level `reverse` index (`{jira_key: local_id}`). The `bindings` section is ~94% of the file, so every call pays for building the full document. Callers: `binding_jira_key_map` (once per `search_state`) and `_resolve_via_binding_store` (once per Jira-key-shaped id in `resolve_ticket_id`). Measured on a copy of the live store (23.5 MB, 5,664 bindings): 67.1 MB tracemalloc peak per call, and a long-lived process (MCP server) re-parses the unchanged file on every call.

## Approach
Operator decision 2026-11-02 (final): option B + C.

- **B — reverse-only validating parse.** Replace the whole-file `json.load` with `json.load(f, object_pairs_hook=_keep_reverse_only)`. The hook keeps a JSON object whose values contain no object (a leaf, e.g. the `reverse` map itself) as a plain dict, and reduces any object that contains a nested object to just its `reverse` key. So binding entries and the `bindings` map are dropped as soon as each is parsed, while the top-level document keeps `reverse`. The parse still validates the WHOLE file, so the documented corrupt-store contract holds: any JSON syntax error anywhere (including a git conflict marker inside `bindings`) makes the loader return `{}` and never raise. Also catch `ValueError` (covers `UnicodeDecodeError`) and treat a non-object top level as `{}`, so "never raises" holds for those inputs too.
- **C — per-process cache.** Memoize the parsed reverse map in a module-level dict keyed by bindings path, storing `(mtime_ns, size, reverse)` taken from `os.fstat` of the opened file (the same freshness token as `_TOML_CACHE` in `src/rebar/_config_sources.py` and `_file_token` in `src/rebar/config.py`). A call whose current `os.stat` token matches the stored one returns the cached map without opening the file; a changed mtime or size re-parses. A missing file returns `{}` and is not cached. Add `reset_binding_reverse_cache()` and call it from the existing autouse `_reset_config_cache` fixture in `tests/conftest.py` so no cached map leaks across tests (no new autouse fixture). The cached map is shared and treated as read-only by both in-module callers (neither mutates it).
- **Other readers, out of scope:** `audit_binding_drift` (`src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge_fsck_drift.py`) iterates every entry of `bindings`, and `BindingRepository` (`src/rebar/reconciler/binding_repository.py`) must round-trip the whole document; a reverse-only parse cannot serve either, so they keep the full load.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_ids.py` — the hook, the cache, `reset_binding_reverse_cache()`, and the rewritten `_load_binding_reverse`.
- `tests/conftest.py` — clear the new cache in the existing `_reset_config_cache` autouse fixture.
- `tests/scripts/reducer/test_ticket_alias_backfill.py` — new tests beside the existing corrupt-store test.

## Testing
- Map identity: `binding_jira_key_map` on a fixture store with nested binding entries, `comment_ids`, and `version` returns the same map as the old whole-file load.
- Corrupt store: a git conflict marker inside the `bindings` section yields `{}` from `_load_binding_reverse` and `None` from `_resolve_via_binding_store`; the existing `test_resolver_jira_key_corrupt_bindings_file_returns_none` still passes. Non-object top level (`[]`) and invalid UTF-8 yield `{}`.
- Cache: two calls on an unchanged file parse once (patch `json.load` in `rebar._ids` with a counting wrapper); a rewrite with a changed size, and one with the same size but a forced different mtime (`os.utime` with `ns=`), are each picked up on the next call.
- Memory: tracemalloc peak of `binding_jira_key_map` before and after on a synthetic store shaped like the live one (~5,600 bindings with nested `baseline` entries, ~23 MB), each measured in a fresh process; numbers recorded in a ticket comment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `_load_binding_reverse` parses with a reverse-only `object_pairs_hook` and returns the same `reverse` map as a whole-file `json.load` on a fixture of the live shape.
- [x] A git conflict marker inside the `bindings` section makes `_load_binding_reverse` return `{}` without raising, covered by a new test; `test_resolver_jira_key_corrupt_bindings_file_returns_none` still passes.
- [x] Repeated calls on an unchanged `bindings.json` parse it once per process, covered by a test.
- [x] A rewritten `bindings.json` (changed size, or same size with changed mtime) is read on the next call, covered by a test.
- [x] The cache is cleared between tests by the existing `_reset_config_cache` autouse fixture.
- [x] Before/after tracemalloc peak of `binding_jira_key_map` on a synthetic store of the live shape is recorded on this ticket.
- [x] `make lint` (including the complexity and mechanism-delta ratchets, exit 0) and `make typecheck` pass.
